item.description:
First release of Shift.
- Run several coding tasks in parallel with Claude Code or Codex, each in its own Git worktree, branch and dev server. - Test each task in your browser, look at the diff, and merge into your base branch. - Answer agent questions and approvals from the app; get notified when a task is ready. - Push merged work to your remote.
- Signed and notarized by Apple: Shift now opens without a security warning. - The push button stays next to the task list when no task is selected.

- Attach files and images by dropping them on a prompt field. The agent gets their file paths. - App projects use a build command in place of a dev server. The task's Build button builds the app and opens it. - Drag projects in the sidebar to reorder them. - Right-click a project to open it in your editor or in Finder. - Task rows resize when the agent's description comes in. - Task list sections have more space between them. - Diff change counts use a smaller monospaced font.

- Drop any file on a prompt to attach it, and paste images or files straight from the clipboard - See how much of Claude Code's or Codex's usage limit you have left in the bottom bar - Switching a project to App build fills in its build command for you - ⌘, opens the current project's settings - "Open in" menus show Finder once and now include Terminal - Project icons show up for more projects, including Icon Composer icons and monorepos - Task rows are all the same height - The project title in the task list resizes to fit when you switch projects

- Drop any file on a prompt to attach it, and paste images or files straight from the clipboard - See how much of Claude Code's or Codex's usage limit you have left in the bottom bar - Switching a project to App build fills in its build command for you - ⌘, opens the current project's settings - "Open in" menus show Finder once and now include Terminal - Project icons show up for more projects, including Icon Composer icons and monorepos - Task rows are all the same height - The project title in the task list resizes to fit when you switch projects

- Pick the model for Claude Code or Codex in project settings or the bottom bar - Each task keeps its own base branch, and changing it moves only that task's work - Create a new branch from the base picker with New Branch… - Push a task's branch to origin from the More menu, or automatically when it finishes - Agent output is readable now, with a Raw toggle for the original stream - Your new task draft stays put when a task finishes or moves to another section - Merging no longer deletes work when a task's base is set to its own branch

- The server link shows Starting, Running, Not responding or Stopped, based on whether the server actually answers. - A server that stops responding offers Log and Restart, and logs open scrolled to the end. - The globe shows a spinner while the base server starts, and opens the browser once the server is ready. - If a server ends up on a different address, the globe opens that one, or tells you the server did not start. - Adding a folder that is not a Git repository offers to initialize Git for you. - Server, merge and task action buttons are taller, with rounded corners.

- Unsent text in the new task field is kept per project. Switching projects shows a blank field, and coming back brings your draft and attachments back. - Each task keeps its own unsent prompt or answer when you switch to another task. - The suggested dev server command now gives Vite and Astro projects their task's port.
